disposition_reason: Table 3 prints per-brand concentrations of seven metals in ten energy drinks bought in Tanzania.

study.design: Market survey, one sample per brand of ten energy drinks (seven local, three imported)
study.origin: S1-S7 locally manufactured in Tanzania; S8-S10 imported
study.method: Microwave wet digestion (EPA 3052); flame AAS (Thermo iCE 3300)
study.qa: Blanks, external calibration, spiked samples and a recovery study stated but recoveries not reported; no CRM

controls.control: origin: locally manufactured vs imported energy drinks
controls.outcome: Authors report no marked distinction; Cd 0.12-0.15 mg/L in local S1-S7 vs 0.09-0.12 mg/L in imported S8-S10

unresolved: Cadmium at 0.09-0.15 mg/L by flame AAS is 1-3 orders of magnitude above the other energy-drink studies the authors tabulate (Table 4); no CRM or recovery values are shown, so the cadmium values are plausibly affected by matrix or calibration problems.
Hazard quotients, EDI and ILCR (Tables 6-8) are derived values, not concentrations; not extracted.
Sample collection dates are not reported.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: WHO limits used as comparator (Cd 0.003, Pb 0.01, Ni 0.07, Cr 0.05, Cu 2 mg/L)
